articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated for the purpose of determining the functions and powers and status of the chief accountant, and giving play to the role of the chief accountant in strengthening economic management and improving economic efficiency.

Article 2 State-owned large and medium-sized enterprises shall set up the post of chief accountant; institutions and competent business departments may, as needed and subject to approval, set up the post of chief accountant.
The setting up, functions and powers, appointment and removal, and rewards and penalties of the chief accountant shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations.

Article 3 The chief accountant is a member of the administrative leadership of the unit, assists the principal administrative leader of the unit in his/her work, and is directly responsible to the principal administrative leader of the unit.

Article 4 In any unit where the post of chief accountant is set up, no deputy post that overlaps with the functions and powers of the chief accountant shall be established among the members of the administrative leadership of the unit.

Article 5 The chief accountant shall organize and lead the work of financial management, cost management, budget management, accounting and accounting supervision of the unit, and participate in the analysis and decision-making of important economic issues of the unit.

Article 6 The chief accountant shall specifically organize the unit to implement the relevant state laws, regulations, guidelines, policies and systems on finance and economics, and protect state property.
The functions and powers of the chief accountant shall be protected by state law. The principal administrative leader of the unit shall support and ensure that the chief accountant exercises his/her functions and powers according to law.

Article 8 The chief accountant shall be responsible for putting forward plans for the establishment of the finance and accounting organ of the unit and the staffing of accounting personnel, and for the establishment and appointment of accounting professional posts; organizing the professional training and assessment of accounting personnel; and supporting accounting personnel to exercise their functions and powers according to law.

Article 9 The chief accountant shall assist the principal administrative leader of the unit in making decisions on issues such as the production and operation of enterprises, the business development of administrative institutions, and investment in capital construction.
The chief accountant shall participate in the formulation of plans for new product development, technological transformation, scientific and technological research, prices of goods (services), and wages and bonuses; and shall participate in the study and review of major economic contracts and economic agreements.

Article 10 The chief accountant may stop or correct any act that violates the state laws, regulations, guidelines, policies and systems on finance and economics, and any act that may cause economic losses or waste. Where the stopping or correction is ineffective, the matter shall be submitted to the principal administrative leader of the unit for handling.
If the principal administrative leader of the unit does not agree with the chief accountant's opinion on the handling of the act mentioned in the preceding paragraph, the chief accountant shall implement the relevant provisions of the Accounting Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 11 The chief accountant shall have the authority to organize the economic accounting, financial accounting, and cost management work of the various functional departments and directly subordinate grassroots organizations of the unit.

Article 12 The chief accountant shall be in charge of approving financial revenues and expenditures. Except that routine financial revenues and expenditures may be approved by the head of the financial accounting institution or other designated personnel authorized by the chief accountant, major financial revenues and expenditures shall be approved by the chief accountant or submitted by the chief accountant to the principal administrative leader of the unit for approval.

Article 13 Budgets, plans for financial revenues and expenditures, plans for costs and expenses, credit plans, special financial reports, and final accounting statements shall be signed by the chief accountant.
Major business plans, economic contracts, economic agreements, etc., involving financial revenues and expenditures, shall be countersigned by the chief accountant within the unit.

Article 14 The appointment, promotion, transfer, reward, and punishment of accounting personnel shall be subject to prior consultation with the chief accountant. The candidates for the head of the financial accounting institution or the accounting supervisor shall be subject to professional assessment by the chief accountant and shall be examined and approved in accordance with relevant regulations.

Article 15 The chief accountant of an enterprise shall be nominated by the principal administrative leader of the unit and shall be appointed or employed by the competent government department; the procedure for removal or dismissal shall be the same as that for appointment or employment.
The chief accountant of a public institution or a competent business department shall be appointed or employed in accordance with the authority for management of cadres; the procedure for removal or dismissal shall be the same as that for appointment or employment.

Article 19 If the principal administrative leader of a unit obstructs the chief accountant from exercising his or her authority, or retaliates against or indirectly retaliates against the chief accountant, the competent superior unit shall impose administrative sanctions depending on the circumstances. If the circumstances are serious enough to constitute a crime, the judicial authority shall investigate criminal liability according to law.
Article 20 If urban or rural collective-owned enterprises or institutions need to set up the post of chief accountant, they shall refer to these Regulations for implementation.

All provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities directly under the Central Government, and departments of the State Council may formulate implementing measures in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations and in light of the actual conditions of their respective regions and departments.
These Regulations shall be interpreted by the Ministry of Finance.

These Regulations shall come into force as of the date of promulgation. The provisions on chief accountants in the "Several Provisions (Draft) on the Establishment of Chief Accountants in State-owned Industrial and Transportation Enterprises" approved by the State Council on October 18, 1963 and transmitted by the State Economic Commission and the Ministry of Finance, and in the "Regulations on the Functions and Powers of Accounting Personnel" promulgated by the State Council on September 12, 1978 shall be abolished simultaneously.
